1	# Creating a command
2	
3	Commands are declared with `defineCommand`, `defineOption` and `defineArgument`, on top of `cliparse`. Options and arguments are validated and parsed by [Zod](https://zod.dev) schemas, and their types flow into the handler. The reasons behind this design are explained in [ADR 0001](../adr/adr-0001-rework-file-structure.md).
4	
5	Before writing a command, look at a similar one and copy its naming, file layout, output format and error messages. `src/commands/drain/` is a good example of a command group with shared arguments and options.
6	
7	## Example
8	
9	A fictional `clever coffee brew <blend>` subcommand, part of a `coffee` group (neither exists in the CLI). The `<blend>` argument is shared by several `coffee` subcommands, so it lives in `coffee.args.js`:
10	
11	```js
12	// src/commands/coffee/coffee.args.js
13	import { z } from 'zod';
14	import { defineArgument } from '../../lib/define-argument.js';
15	
16	export const blendArg = defineArgument({
17	  schema: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, 'Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes'),
18	  description: 'Blend of coffee',
19	  placeholder: 'blend',
20	});
21	```
22	
23	`--shots`, `--milk` and `--topping` are only used by this subcommand, so they are defined inline. `--format` comes from `global.options.js`:
24	
25	```js
26	// src/commands/coffee/coffee.brew.command.js
27	import { z } from 'zod';
28	import { brewCoffee } from '../../clever-client/coffee.js';
29	import { defineCommand } from '../../lib/define-command.js';
30	import { defineOption } from '../../lib/define-option.js';
31	import { Logger } from '../../logger.js';
32	import { sendToApi } from '../../models/send-to-api.js';
33	import { humanJsonOutputFormatOption } from '../global.options.js';
34	import { blendArg } from './coffee.args.js';
35	
36	export const coffeeBrewCommand = defineCommand({
37	  description: 'Brew a coffee',
38	  since: null,
39	  options: {
40	    shots: defineOption({
41	      name: 'shots',
42	      schema: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(4).default(1),
43	      description: 'Number of espresso shots',
44	      aliases: ['s'],
45	      placeholder: 'shots',
46	    }),
47	    milk: defineOption({
48	      name: 'milk',
49	      schema: z.enum(['none', 'whole', 'oat']).default('none'),
50	      description: 'Kind of milk',
51	      placeholder: 'milk',
52	    }),
53	    toppings: defineOption({
54	      name: 'topping',
55	      schema: z
56	        .union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())])
57	        .transform((value) => (typeof value === 'string' ? [value] : value))
58	        .optional(),
59	      description: 'Topping to add. Multiple --topping can be passed',
60	      placeholder: 'topping',
61	    }),
62	    format: humanJsonOutputFormatOption,
63	  },
64	  args: [blendArg],
65	  async handler(options, blend) {
66	    const { shots, milk, toppings, format } = options;
67

# 📖 `clever k8s` command reference

> [!NOTE]
> 🧪 **Experimental**: This command may change or be removed in future versions.
> Enable with: `clever features enable k8s`

## ➡️ `clever k8s` <kbd>Since 4.3.0</kbd>

Manage Kubernetes clusters

```bash
clever k8s
```

## ➡️ `clever k8s activity` <kbd>Since unreleased</kbd>

Show recent deployment events of a Kubernetes cluster

```bash
clever k8s activity <cluster-id|cluster-name> [options]
```

### 📥 Arguments

|Name|Description|
|---|---|
|`cluster-id|cluster-name`|Kubernetes cluster ID or name|

I added `clever k8s quota`, but I haven't run it against the real API, so the output is untested. `npm run fix-all` and `npm run validate` pass (lint, format, types, docs check). I couldn't test the new command: the experimental features file I created for the run only turned on `k8s` after the command had already failed, because dependencies weren't installed. I never retried the command after `npm ci`. `node bin/clever.js k8s quota --help` printed the general help instead of the command's own help, which I didn't look into.

- **What it does:** it shows the Kubernetes quotas of an organisation. The API serves quotas per organisation, not per cluster, so the command takes `--org` and `--format json` and no cluster argument.
- **Output:** the default view prints a "Kubernetes quotas" table with one row per entry in the response's `quotas` field. If there are none, it prints "No Kubernetes quota found for this organisation". With `--format json` it prints the raw response.
- **Unknown response shape:** I don't know what the `quotas` field contains. Nothing in the repo describes it, so the table is generic. It would be worth running the command on a test account and tuning the layout.
- **Implementation:** I reused the existing `k8sGetQuota` helper in `src/lib/k8s.js` and the `getK8sQuota` endpoint, which nothing was calling before. The command is in `src/commands/k8s/k8s.quota.command.js` and registered in `global.commands.js`. It has `since: null`, as for any new command.
- **Generated docs:** `npm run docs` updated `k8s.docs.md` and `skills/clever-tools/references/full-documentation.md`.
- **Reverted file:** `fix-all` reformatted `.claude/settings.json`, which has nothing to do with this change, so I reverted it.

I haven't committed anything.
